solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Surprise attack by former president on America

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: George Bush, either of two former US presidents

explanation.surface: A news report of an ex-president turning on his own country with a sudden assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts the president after AM.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a sudden attack sprung from hiding, a classic surprise assault.

clue.text: Suitable program location to store zero

indicators.note: the two joined pieces hold, or keep, the next piece between them

parts.note: an app is a computer program
a site is a place or location
O looks like the figure nought

explanation.surface: Talk of finding a good place in software to save a value of zero.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to store' has the program and location hold the zero between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means apt or well suited to the occasion, a close synonym.

clue.text: Delight in mentioning insolent manner of worker?

indicators.note: mentioning means saying out loud, so the sound of the phrase gives the entry

parts.note: a worker is a bee, and an insolent manner is attitude, giving 'bee attitude'

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in describing an employee's cheeky demeanour.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker is a worker bee, a crossword favourite; 'bee attitude' said aloud gives the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Beatitude is supreme blessedness or bliss, a lofty word for great happiness.

clue.text: Mark left by The Sound of Music in Jamaica

indicators.note: a borrowed film title, here simply signalling how a word is pronounced

parts.note: ska is a Jamaican music style, forerunner of reggae

explanation.surface: A film title, The Sound of Music, seems to have left its mark in Jamaica.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the entry is said exactly like SKA.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark a healed wound leaves behind on the skin.

clue.text: He's likely to lose, according to boxer?

parts.note: under means according to, as in 'under the rules'
a boxer is a breed of dog, the question mark flagging the example

explanation.surface: A boxer's pre-fight prediction about which contestant will probably be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not the fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdog is the competitor expected to be beaten in a contest, the outsider.

clue.text: Close relationship is something fitting for retirement

parts.note: nigh means near or close
a tie is a bond or relationship

explanation.surface: An intimate bond turns out to be well suited to life after work.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement here is going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightgown is clothing worn, or fitted, when one retires to bed for the night.

clue.text: Film about Greek musician and creator of gospel

indicators.note: the film's title goes around, or about, the musician's name

parts.note: E.T. is Spielberg's film about an extra-terrestrial
Vangelis was the Greek composer of the Chariots of Fire score

explanation.surface: A movie about a Greek performer who also wrote gospel music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VANGELIS inside E.T.; gospel means a Gospel of the New Testament, not the music.
explanation.definitionFit: The four Evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John, are credited with writing the Gospels.

clue.text: Sketch concealing son's stoop

indicators.note: concealing means hiding a letter away so it no longer shows

parts.note: a design is a drawing or sketch
S is the abbreviation for son, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A drawing hides the son's posture of bending forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing' removes S from DESIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop to something is to condescend, lowering oneself to do it, a synonym.

clue.text: Screen reporter's question thoroughly

indicators.note: a reporter's version of a word is how it is spoken

parts.note: to grill someone is to question them intensely

explanation.surface: Instructions to vet a journalist's question with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reporter's' signals a word said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating of bars over a window or opening works as a protective screen.

clue.text: Opportune issue raised by empty library

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to emit is to issue or give out

indicators.note: an empty word loses everything inside, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A pressing topic brought up by a deserted library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reads the issue upwards in this down clue; 'empty' keeps only the outside letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune and timely both describe something occurring at a convenient, well-chosen moment.

clue.text: Calming concerns of nervous capital leads to new guidelines

indicators.note: nervous, as in jittery, shows the letters are shaken up
the leads of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Easing financial worries that jittery capital will bring new regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' gives PLACATI from CAPITAL; 'leads to' gives NG.
explanation.definitionFit: Placating someone means soothing or appeasing them, so it is a form of calming.

clue.text: Bail suspect with one good reason for doing so?

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means doubtful, so the letters are not to be trusted in order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Releasing a suspect on bail for a decent reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges BAIL to ALIB. A suspect with a sound excuse, such as being elsewhere, ought to be bailed.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is proof of being elsewhere, the best reason a suspect could have for being freed.

clue.text: Reduce size of corporation?

parts.note: corporation is an old jocular word for a big belly, so shrinking it means dieting

explanation.surface: A business looks to downsize its workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation is old British slang for a paunch, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose weight by dieting makes the waistline, the paunch, thinner.

clue.text: Append a line by writer associated with Department of Defense?

indicators.note: the writer comes beside, and here before, the rest

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
to tag on is to append or add

explanation.surface: Instructions for adding a line from an author linked to the US defence ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: The US Department of Defense is headquartered in the Pentagon, a five-sided building.
explanation.definitionFit: Five-sided shapes recall the Pentagon, home of the US military, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Attacker doing time felt wronged

parts.note: inside is slang for being in prison

indicators.note: wronged suggests the letters have been treated badly and knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A prisoner believes he was treated unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wronged' rearranges FELT into LEFT. In older football formations this forward played left of centre.
explanation.definitionFit: In football an attacking forward position, between the outside left and the centre forward.

clue.text: Time travel initially banned in contest

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is barred from it

parts.note: a journey is a trip or travel

explanation.surface: Time travel being prohibited from a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially banned' removes J from JOURNEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourney is a tournament, originally a medieval jousting competition between knights.

clue.text: Pastry base with crushed garlic's not good

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

indicators.note: crushed garlic is pounded into a new form, so the letters are mixed
not says a piece must be left out of the mixture

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe-s linking it to what follows

explanation.surface: A recipe in which crushed garlic is wrong for a pastry base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' signals the mixing and 'not' removes the good from it; base is the mathematical constant e.
explanation.definitionFit: A long choux bun filled with cream and topped with chocolate icing is a classic pastry.

clue.text: Crude, popular lament: Burying the Unknown Soldier

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: burying puts a letter out of sight, so it is lost from the word

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem, a lament
in algebra Y is an unknown quantity
a soldier ant is a kind of worker ant

explanation.surface: A tasteless pop song mourning at the burial of the Unknown Soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burying' removes Y from ELEGY, leaving ELEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude in the sense of lacking grace or refinement; clumsy, unpolished.

clue.text: Object to confuse debugger

indicators.note: to confuse is to mix up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An aim of muddling the person fixing the code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confuse' rearranges DEBUGGER.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge something is to resent or object to it grudgingly.

clue.text: Clubs say accepting racket is giving up

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds another

parts.note: eg (for example) means say
din is a loud racket

explanation.surface: Golf clubs taking in a tennis racket means quitting golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' has the abbreviation for say hold the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or ground is to surrender it, the sense of handing over.

clue.text: Refuse to get on with actress having been snubbed earlier

indicators.note: says the cut actress comes before the next piece
snubbed means cut short, so the last letter is docked

parts.note: Greta Garbo, the Swedish film actress
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Declining to work with a star after being slighted by her before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been snubbed' docks O from GARBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is rubbish or waste, the household trash.

clue.text: Crowd round saint that is interrupting father endlessly

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into the middle of something
the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to beget is to father a child
ie is the Latin abbreviation id est, that is

explanation.surface: A holy figure being swamped, interrupting a priest's endless talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts BEGET to BEGE; 'interrupting' puts SIE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To besiege is to surround and hem in, as an army or a mob of reporters does.

clue.text: Trouble for member of British workers' organisation

parts.note: a trade union represents workers

explanation.surface: Difficulties for someone who belongs to a British trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: Member here is a limb, specifically the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful swelling on the big toe joint is an affliction of the foot, a bodily member.

clue.text: Do well without having succeeded in conforming to accepted norms

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: to prosper is to do well or thrive
S is a genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: Thriving without ever quite succeeding in fitting in with society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes S from PROSPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper behaviour is correct and respectable, matching what society expects.

clue.text: Misleading article about dead husband going astray

parts.note: re means about or concerning
erring means straying from the right path

explanation.surface: A deceptive newspaper report about a late husband who had been unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: A false clue that draws attention away from the truth; article here means item.

clue.text: Doc perhaps died following cold's recurrence

indicators.note: recurrence suggests running back, so the word reverses

parts.note: raw means cold, as in a raw winter day
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: A physician perhaps died after a cold came back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrence' reverses RAW to WAR. Doc is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White.
explanation.definitionFit: Doc is one of the seven little men in Snow White, an example of the class.

clue.text: Sport is ultimately like going into battle

indicators.note: one piece entering inside another

parts.note: war is battle or fighting

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter

explanation.surface: A competitive game being compared to warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives E; 'going into' puts it inside WAR. Sport is the verb, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport a garment is to wear it showily, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Dancing characters in the middle of silver screen

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so they are rearranged
the letters inside a word, without its ends

explanation.surface: Dancers occupying the centre of a cinema screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in the middle of' takes ILVE from SILVER and 'Dancing' rearranges it. Silver screen hides the definition, screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a cloth that hides or conceals, as a screen does.

clue.text: Newspaper article declared end to hostilities

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: a piece is an article in a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper report announcing that fighting has stopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declared' signals that PIECE is said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Peace is the state reached when war and fighting cease.

clue.text: Noted prior to supply ideas for opening of abbey

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: supply read as supplely, bending flexibly, so the letters move

explanation.surface: Plans to provide suggestions for the launch of a monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' rearranges IDEAS into ESAID; 'opening of' gives A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid describes something mentioned earlier, previously stated in the text.

clue.text: Renewed attack put off Revolutionary Guards

indicators.note: guards means holds protectively around something
a revolution turns round, so the word reverses

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: Iran's Revolutionary Guards discouraged a fresh assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reverses the discouraging word into RETED; 'Guards' has it hold the attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To refit something is to repair or re-equip it, making it renewed.

clue.text: Sale item charges 60% of cheap dress

indicators.note: one piece charges, or rushes, into another
sixty percent of the word, the first three of five letters

parts.note: a lot is an item at an auction sale

explanation.surface: An item at a sale charges a price below the cheap rate for a frock.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' keeps three of the five letters; 'charges' sends the sale item into them.
explanation.definitionFit: To clothe someone is to dress them, putting garments on them.
